questions.question: The demo mints API tokens but has no Supabase project, so `make cashback-demo` cannot sign a *browser* in — its own closing message says so, and F8's browser test needs exactly that. How should a session be established locally and in CI?

options.label: Build the shell token-exchange, flag-gated (Recommended)
options.description: Build the design's second path now — a route that takes a JWKS-verified bearer token and mints a session of our own — behind an env flag that is off in production. The demo and Playwright turn it on; the shell *button* stays disabled with its copy until there is a shell. One mechanism serves the demo, the test, and production later.
options.preview:
POST /auth/shell   (enabled only when SHELL_TOKEN_EXCHANGE=1)
  body: token=<jwt from $TMP/reader.token>
  -> verify against JWKS_URL
  -> set our own httpOnly session cookie
  -> 303 to ?next=

production:  flag unset -> 404, button stays disabled
demo / e2e:  flag set   -> Playwright signs in in one POST

options.label: Point the demo at a real Supabase project
options.description: Give scripts/cashback_demo.sh real PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL / ANON_KEY for the nonprod project and use the true magic-link flow. Most faithful, but needs credentials in CI and a mailbox the test can read — the nonprod mailer is rate-limited.

options.label: A dev-only sign-in route

# Finishing the cashback member frontend (F1–F9)

## Context

`docs/master-prompts/cashback-frontend.md` on `origin/main` is the brief: bring
the member-facing cashback screens in `web/` to the point where one real person
can sign up, opt in, click out to a Linkwise retailer and watch a pending entry
appear in their wallet.

The backend is largely built. What the web cannot do is **sign a member in** —
`pages/[lang]/signin.astro` exists with every control `disabled` and says so on
its own face. Every cashback surface is already wired to an API it can never
present a member token to. Backend gaps B1–B6 (#544–#548) are being worked in
parallel; this plan builds against the documented contract rather than waiting
on them, and says explicitly which proof waits on which gap.

Three founder decisions taken this session:

- **Demo/CI sign-in**: build the design's second path — a route that exchanges a
  bearer token for a session of our own — behind an env flag that is off in
  production. The shell *button* stays disabled with its copy until there is a
  shell. The demo and the browser test use the route.
- **Terms**: add a `/{lang}/terms` route so the opt-in cites a readable document.
- **B4**: leave the web's routes on `/api/`; the deploy side narrows the edge
  matcher to `/api/v1/*`. Click-out is proved locally now, on QA when B4 lands.

## Starting state

`xcoder/member-signin` is **fully merged into `origin/main`** (PR #531) and ~30
commits behind it. Every branch below starts fresh from `origin/main`. The
working tree's modified `.claude/`, `.githooks/` and `.entire/` entries are local
tooling and are never committed.

**No issue exists for any of F1–F9.** Each PR below needs one opened first
(`gh issue create`), and dependent chains are bound with `gh stack`.

## What the survey established

**The auth seam already fits a member.** `resolveEditorSession(request, cookies)`
→ `editorSessionFrom(user, token)` → `{ displayName, email, role, token,
authenticated }`, filed in a `WeakMap<Request, …>` and read back synchronously by
`editorSession(request)` (`lib/editorial/session.ts:270–286`). There is **no
`Astro.locals` and no `App.Locals` type**. `roleOf` collapses anything that is
not `editor`/`operator` to `reader` — which is what a member is. `@supabase/ssr`
already exposes `signInWithOtp` and `verifyOtp`; **no new package is needed for
F1.** The middleware never redirects and does not match `/{lang}/signin`.

**`api/tour/[tour].ts` is the pattern** for a route that must keep a bearer token
server-side: it calls `resolveEditorSession` directly rather than trusting the
middleware to have matched its path.

**The design canvas** (26 boards, artifact `059a20a9-…`) draws SignIn almost
exactly as built — shell button primary, email link secondary, no password, no
"check your email" state. It **draws no opt-in screen and no payout-destination
form anywhere**; it asserts the payout requirement in three places
(`SettingsSeam`: *"Money leaves through it, so it cannot live anywhere but with
the module that moves the money"*) and shows both status chips, but never the
screen between them. Those two screens are mine to design. New screens use
`modernist.css`'s own tokens (`--space-N`, `--color-accent-N`, `--ink-muted`,
`--font-heading`), radius 0, hairline borders, no shadows — as `signin.astro`
already does.

**The contract has drifted, and it breaks a real screen.** Verified against the
Go source, not just the OpenAPI document:

| `types.ts` says | Go actually sends |
|---|---|
| `EntryState` = `…\|'declined'`, no `reserved` | `held pending confirmed reserved paid reversed` (`earnings/state.go:24–40`, migration 0013 check) — no `declined` |
| `PayoutDestination { id, kind, details, verified_at }` | `{ destination_id, kind, verified_at, verified_method, created_at }` — **and the Go comment says "There is no details field and there never will be"** (`payout/handlers.go:430–446`) |
| `Withdrawal { id, destination: {…}, reserved_amount }` | `{ request_id, destination_id, amount, state, requested_at, decided_at, decision_reason, payout_reference }` (`handlers.go:354–370`) |
| destinations/withdrawals paged | both are `{ items }` with **no `next_cursor`** (`handlers.go:385, 475`) |
| `Clickout.expires_at: string` | nullable |
| `Participation` has no `left_at` | `left_at` is required |
| `WalletEntry` | adds `merchant_name_language`, `merchant_name_is_fallback`, `hold_rule`; `merchant_name` nullable |

`withdraw.astro` renders `destination.details` and `reserved_amount`, and
`api.destinations()` unwraps a cursor page. **Against the real API the withdrawal
screen does not work today.** This is why the contract PR comes first.

**The member journey's other holes.** `api.optIn()` has zero call sites and
`t.optIn` is rendered nowhere; the wallet's not-participating band links to the
catalogue (`wallet.astro:242–249`). `participation()` is called only by the
wallet, so a non-participant is offered a click. Every member page collapses 401
into `503 + t.emptyQueue` ("nothing open in this list") through one broad catch.
`[slug].astro:82` reads `?clickout=<status>` with `.has()` and discards the code.
Only `rates[0]` is clickable. `next_cursor` is read nowhere. `CashbackNav.astro`
is dead code superseded by `MemberBar.astro`.

## The work

Each numbered item is one issue and one PR, several small commits, every
intermediate commit building and passing. Stacks are bound with `gh stack`.

### 0 — The contract, first *(unblocks everything that touches real data)*

`fix(web): the cashback types say what the api actually sends`

Correct `types.ts` against the Go handlers and `api/openapi.json`; make
`destinations()` and `withdrawals()` read `{ items }`; follow through into
`fixtures.ts`, the `entryStates`/`withdrawalStates` records in
`i18n/cashback.ts`, `withdraw.astro` and `wallet.astro`. This is a *correction*
to a hand-written file, not a contract change — the other two places already
agree. Open a **backend** issue for the one real contract gap: `api/openapi.json`
declares no extension members on `Problem`, while the prose and `withdraw.astro`
both rely on `threshold`/`shortfall` on the 409.

### 1 — F1, member sign-in *(a stack of five)*

1. `feat(web): a session resolves wherever a member signs in` — widen
   `isAuthenticatedPath` to `/{lang}/signin`, `/{lang}/register` and `/auth/*`.
   One mechanical commit renaming `EditorSession` → `Session` (it stops being an
   editor's), leaving `editorSession(request)` as the accessor.
2. `feat(web): the email link signs a member in` — a POST branch calling
   `signInWithOtp({ email, options: { emailRedirectTo } })`, guarded by
   `isSameOrigin` (`lib/csrf.ts:53`); a `/auth/confirm` route calling
   `verifyOtp({ token_hash, type })`, which writes the same `@supabase/ssr`
   httpOnly cookies the editor sign-in writes; a `?next=` return path accepting
   same-origin paths only. New `lib/member/strings.ts` copy for sent / expired /
   refused / not-configured, in `el` and `de`. `signin.test.ts` is **rewritten**:
   it asserts the working page as precisely as it now asserts the disabled one,
   and `member/strings.test.ts`'s "no URL, no `mailto:`, no `http`" rule is
   replaced with rules that fit copy that now describes a mechanism.
3. `feat(web): a signed-in member becomes an account` — after a successful
   callback, `POST /api/v1/account` with the member's own token (B1, #544).
   Until B1 lands that answers 404; the route records it and item 3 of F2 renders
   "your membership is being set up" rather than a 503.
4. `feat(web): the app shell exchanges a token for a session` — `/auth/shell`,
   present only when a new optional `SHELL_TOKEN_EXCHANGE` env field is set.
   **It verifies the token by using it**: one call to `GET /participation` with
   that bearer. A 200 or 404 means the api verified it against `JWKS_URL` *and*
   found an `account` row; a 401 refuses. That needs no JWT library (`jose` is
   not installed and this avoids adding it), cannot drift from the api's own
   verification, and proves membership rather than just signature. On acceptance
   the token goes into our own httpOnly `SameSite=Lax` cookie, read back by a new
   `lib/member/session.ts` resolver that tries this cookie first and falls back to
   `resolveEditorSession`. The shell **button stays disabled with its copy**.
   Record plainly that this session does not refresh — the shell re-hands a token.
5. `feat(web): sign-out, and the chrome that names who is signed in` — a sign-out
   POST mirroring the editor's; `MemberBar`'s `aside` naming the signed-in member;
   the front page's disabled button becoming a link, which retires
   `memberStrings.frontPageButtonState` and its assertion.
6. `feat(web): signing up is the same flow` — `register.astro`'s disabled account
   fields give way to the one email field; the consent panel is untouched.

### 2 — F2, gating

`feat(web): a cashback page without a member sends them to sign in`

One `requireMember(Astro)` used by every `/{lang}/{place}/cashback/…` page: no
session ⇒ redirect to `/{lang}/signin?next=…`; a 401 from the api ⇒ the same;
`/ops` without the operator role ⇒ a 403 page rather than chrome around an empty
queue. The broad catch stops collapsing 401 into `t.emptyQueue`, and gains a
member-facing error string of its own.

### 3 — F3, opt-in *(two PRs)*

1. `feat(web): the cashback terms, on their own route` — `/{lang}/terms`, a
   fourth pane in the legal family, rendering against `brand.legal` and citing
   `legal.documents.terms.version`. Nothing brand-shaped is a literal.
2. `feat(web): a member opts in before they can be paid` — a join screen reached
   when `GET /participation` answers 404, posting
   `brand.legal.documents.terms.version` — the same field
   `Participations.Join` compares (`internal/cashback/wallet/participations.go:162`),
   read from the same `brand.json`. `ErrNoBrand`'s 503 says the deployment names
   no brand and does not retry. The wallet's band points here, not at the
   catalogue.

### 4 — F5, click-out *(three PRs)*

1. `fix(web): the click-out failure says which failure it was` — read the status
   in `?clickout=<status>`; distinct copy for 401, 409, 429 and 502.
2. `feat(web): no click is offered to a member who has not opted in` — the
   merchant page checks participation, and the click-out endpoint refuses,
   until B3 makes the api refuse too.
3. `feat(web): every published band is clickable, not only the first`.

### 5 — F4 and F6, catalogue and wallet

1. `feat(web): the catalogue reads its next page` — `next_cursor` paging, plus
   the design board's ordering disclosure ("the order follows your language and
   your places; no position is sold"). The real endpoint arrives with B2 (#545);
   the fixture keeps development moving meanwhile.
2. `fix(web): the wallet's entry count stops capping at one page`.

### 6 — F7, payout destination

`feat(web): a member adds a payout destination`

`POST /payout-destinations` added to `types.ts`, `api.ts` and the fixtures
(`{ kind, details }` in, a destination with `verified_at: null` out); a screen to
add one; an "awaiting verification" state; `withdraw.astro:301–315`'s dead end
replaced by a link to it. Verification itself is B6 (#548) and is not needed
before the first transaction.

### 7 — F8, the end-to-end test

`test(web): the member journey, in a browser`

Playwright is greenfield — nothing in the repo or CI installs a browser. Tests
live in `web/e2e/`, outside vitest's `src/**/*.test.ts` glob, with their own
config and a new CI job. The test runs against `make cashback-demo` (which starts
Postgres-backed api, the JWKS stand-in minting `$TMP/reader.token`, and `astro
dev` on :4321) and signs in through `/auth/shell` with that token. It walks
sign-in → opt-in → click-out.

### F9 — carried by every PR

Every new string in `el` and `de`, satisfying `i18n/cashback.test.ts`'s four
rules: same key shape and depth, non-empty, **no `€` and no `EUR`**, and every
interpolating function added to the exercised array. Every new page literal-free
from its first commit — `scripts/lint-brand-literals.sh` is a per-file ratchet and
a file with no budget entry fails on its first hit. Every new logic module added
to `vitest.config.ts`'s coverage `include`, or it escapes the 80% gate silently.

## Files this touches most

- `web/src/lib/cashback/types.ts`, `api.ts`, `fixtures.ts` — the contract
- `web/src/lib/editorial/session.ts`, `supabase.ts`, `web/src/middleware.ts` — the session
- `web/src/lib/member/strings.ts`, `web/src/i18n/cashback.ts`, `web/src/lib/legal/strings.ts` — copy
- `web/src/pages/[lang]/signin.astro`, `register.astro`, and new `/auth/confirm`, `/auth/shell`, `/{lang}/terms`
- `web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/*.astro` and a new join screen
- `web/astro.config.mjs` — one new optional env field
- `scripts/cashback_demo.sh` — set the exchange flag so the demo's pages stop being fixtures

## Verification

Per PR, before pushing:

```sh
cd web && npm ci && npm run check && npm test && npm run build   # CI `frontend`
sh scripts/lint-brand-literals.sh                                # CI `brand-literals`
make ref-lint                                                    # xcoder/<slug>
sh scripts/lint-refs.sh --from-messages origin/main..HEAD
sh scripts/lint-commit-authors.sh origin/main..HEAD
```

End to end, locally:

```sh
make cashback-demo          # api + JWKS stand-in + seeded catalogue + web on :4321
# then, in a browser: sign in via /auth/shell with $TMP/reader.token,
# opt in, open a retailer, click out, read the wallet
```

On QA (`https://ra1ze.com`) once B1/B2/B4 land: sign up with a real email link,
opt in, click out, and record in the PR what was run and what was seen — then
update `docs/master-prompts/cashback-frontend.md` in the same PR.

## What genuinely waits on the backend

- **Sign-up producing a member** waits on B1 (#544). Everything before it builds
  and is proved locally with the demo's minted tokens.
- **The catalogue on the real endpoint** waits on B2 (#545); the page and the
  fixture already work.
- **Click-out proved in a browser on QA** waits on B4 (#546). Proved locally now.
- **The legal pages on QA** wait on B5 (#547).
- **A withdrawal** waits on B6 (#548), and is not part of the first transaction.

cd C:/Users/madym/repos/apivo-news && gh issue create --title "The web's cashback types disagree with what the api sends, and the withdrawal screen cannot work" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
`web/src/lib/cashback/types.ts` is hand-written against the contract and checked
by nothing. It has drifted from the Go handlers far enough that one screen is
broken against a real API rather than merely imprecise.

Verified against the Go source, not only `api/openapi.json`:

| `types.ts` says | the api sends |
|---|---|
| `EntryState` includes `declined`, omits `reserved` | `held pending confirmed reserved paid reversed` — `internal/cashback/earnings/state.go:24-40`, and migration 0013's `entry_state_known` check. There is no `declined`. |
| `PayoutDestination { id, kind, details, verified_at }` | `{ destination_id, kind, verified_at, verified_method, created_at }` — `internal/cashback/payout/handlers.go:437-446`, whose comment reads "There is no details field and there never will be". |
| `Withdrawal { id, destination: {...}, reserved_amount }` | `{ request_id, destination_id, amount, state, requested_at, decided_at, decision_reason, payout_reference }` — `handlers.go:354-370`. |
| both lists are cursor pages | both answer `{ items }` with no `next_cursor` — `handlers.go:385` and `:475`. |
| `Clickout.expires_at: string` | nullable. |
| `Participation` has no `left_at` | `left_at` is required. |
| `WalletEntry` | adds `merchant_name_language`, `merchant_name_is_fallback` and `hold_rule`, and `merchant_name` is nullable. |

The consequence is not theoretical. `withdraw.astro` renders
`destination.details` and `reserved_amount` on every row of a member's
withdrawal history, and `api.destinations()` unwraps a cursor page that the
endpoint does not return. Against the deployed api that screen renders blanks.

This is a correction to the one place that was never checked. `http-api.md` and
`api/openapi.json` already agree with the Go; only the TypeScript does not.

Fix `types.ts`, then follow it through `api.ts`, `fixtures.ts`, the
`entryStates`/`withdrawalStates` records in `web/src/i18n/cashback.ts`, and the
two pages that read the changed fields.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

cd C:/Users/madym/repos/apivo-news && cat > /tmp/issue_ops.json <<'JSONEOF'
{
  "title": "GET /ops/withdrawals is called by the operator queue and is not implemented",
  "body": "`web/src/lib/cashback/api.ts:389` calls `GET /api/v1/cashback/ops/withdrawals?state=awaiting_approval`, and `web/src/pages/ops/withdrawals.astro` renders the queue from it.

The route does not exist. `internal/cashback/ops/handler.go:83-98` registers only the three decisions:

```
"POST " + Prefix + "withdrawals/{id}/approve": h.approveWithdrawal,
"POST " + Prefix + "withdrawals/{id}/reject":  h.rejectWithdrawal,
"POST " + Prefix + "withdrawals/{id}/settle":  h.settleWithdrawal,
```

`api/openapi.json` carries the same three and no listing.

This is the same shape of gap as #545: documented in the contract's operator section, called by the web, absent from the api. C-4 says a named human approves every payout — and the screen that names them cannot list what is waiting.

The member-side counterpart `GET /withdrawals` exists (`internal/cashback/payout/handlers.go:385`) and answers `{ items }` with rows of `request_id`, `destination_id`, `amount`, `state`, `requested_at`, `decided_at`, `decision_reason`, `payout_reference`. An operator queue needs the account behind each row as well, which the member view deliberately omits.

Until it lands the operator withdrawal queue is a fixture-only screen."
}
JSONEOF
gh api repos/Nomos-N4s/apivo-news/issues --input /tmp/issue_ops.json --jq '"CREATED #\(.number) \(.html_url)"' 2>&1 | tail -2
cat > /tmp/issue_problem.json <<'JSONEOF'
{
  "title": "api/openapi.json declares no extension members on Problem, so the withdrawal 409 is undocumented",
  "body": "`specs/002-apivo-cashback-alpha/contracts/http-api.md` says a withdrawal refused below the threshold answers 409 with `threshold` and `shortfall` as RFC 9457 extension members, and `web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/withdraw.astro:117-139` builds the member's refusal sentence out of exactly those two figures.

`api/openapi.json`'s `Problem` schema declares `type`, `title`, `status` and `detail` and nothing else. A client generated from the document would not know the figures exist, and the CI validation cannot notice if they stop being sent.

Add the extension members the contract promises — `code`, `threshold`, `shortfall`, `confirmed`, `requested` — to the `Problem` schema, so the three places that describe this API agree."
}
JSONEOF

is written in, whether that language is a fallback, and the rule holding a
held entry back. WalletEntry declared none of the four, so the page could not

    there was no click, so there is no route back to a shop (FR-034). The

  * a name that answered in the retailer's own language is labelled, as the
    catalogue already labels it (US5 scenario 2), instead of being passed
    off as the member's own language.
  * a held entry names the rule holding it. "In review" alone does not tell
    a member whether the review is about them.

The preview gains a held entry and a hand-attributed one, because a fixture
set that never produces the null is a fixture set that lets a blank line

nothing to do with the place axis a member browses under. Terms is the

fix(web): a payout destination is a rail and a date, not a masked account (#554)

PayoutDestination declared `id` and a `details` string described as a masked
IBAN. The api has never sent either. It sends destination_id, kind,
verified_at, verified_method and created_at, and the handler says why in as
many words: "There is no details field and there never will be" - the account
lives where this service cannot read it (ADR-0003), and an endpoint echoing it
would be the leak the arrangement exists to prevent.

So the withdrawal screen was printing `undefined` in a monospace span on every
destination it offered and on every past request, against any real
deployment. It now names a destination by what the api actually sends: the
rail, and the day it was added. That is enough to tell apart the one or two
destinations anybody has, and it is all there is.

Withdrawal loses `reserved_amount` and the nested destination for the same
reason. The reserved figure belongs to the 201 that commits a member to it -
where the whole-entries rule can surprise them - and not to a historical row,
where the amount is the amount. The destination arrives as an id, which the
page resolves against the member's own list, and says so plainly when a
withdrawal cites one that is no longer there.

WithdrawalForApproval is left as it stands, with a note: no endpoint serves
it. The operator queue calls GET /ops/withdrawals and the api registers only
the three decisions on that prefix.
MSGEOF

import json, io
body = """Closes #554.

`web/src/lib/cashback/types.ts` is hand-written against the contract and checked by nothing. It had drifted from the Go handlers far enough that a screen was broken against a real API rather than merely imprecise, and the drift was invisible because every page renders from fixtures that agreed with the wrong types.

Each commit corrects one group of fields together with everything that reads them, so every intermediate commit builds and passes.

### What was wrong

| `types.ts` said | the api sends |
|---|---|
| `EntryState` includes `declined`, omits `reserved` | the six in `internal/cashback/earnings/state.go:24-40` and in migration 0013's `entry_state_known` check. There is no `declined`. |
| `WalletEntry` has a non-null `merchant_name` and no language | `merchant_name` is null for a hand-attributed entry (FR-034), and it carries `merchant_name_language`, `merchant_name_is_fallback` and `hold_rule` |
| `Participation` has no `left_at` | `left_at` is required (FR-003) |
| `Clickout.expires_at: string` | nullable — a band with no published end |
| `MerchantDetail` has no `country`, no `terms` | `internal/cashback/catalogue/handlers.go:170-199` sends both |
| `PayoutDestination { id, kind, details, verified_at }` | `{ destination_id, kind, verified_at, verified_method, created_at }` |
| `Withdrawal { id, destination: {...}, reserved_amount }` | `{ request_id, destination_id, amount, state, requested_at, decided_at, decision_reason, payout_reference }` |
| both of those are cursor pages | both answer `{ items }` and no cursor |

### The one that was not cosmetic

`web/src/pages/[lang]/[place]/cashback/withdraw.astro` named every destination by `destination.details`, described in the type as a masked IBAN. The api has never sent that field, and `internal/cashback/payout/handlers.go:430-436` says why in as many words:

> There is no details field and there never will be. What a member sees is which rail it is for and whether it has been proved theirs; the details are somewhere this service cannot read them from (ADR-0003), and an endpoint that echoed them would be the leak the whole arrangement exists to prevent.

So against any real deployment that screen printed `undefined` on every destination it offered and on every past request, and the same on the operator queue.

A destination is now named by what the api actually sends: the rail, and the day it was added. That is enough to tell apart the one or two anybody has, and it is all there is. `Withdrawal` loses `reserved_amount` for a related reason — the reserved figure belongs to the `201` that commits a member to it, where the whole-entries rule can surprise them, and not to a historical row where the amount is the amount.

### Fixtures

The preview gains a held entry naming its hold rule, and one attributed by hand with no retailer at all. A fixture set that never produces the null is a fixture set that lets a blank line reach a member unnoticed.

### Two backend gaps found on the way, filed rather than patched here

- #556 — `GET /ops/withdrawals` is called by the operator queue and is not implemented. Same shape as #545. `WithdrawalForApproval` is left as it stands with a note saying so.
- #557 — `api/openapi.json` declares no extension members on `Problem`, while the contract prose and the withdrawal screen both rely on `threshold` and `shortfall` on the 409.

### Checked

- `npm run check` — 0 errors
- `npm test` — 902 passing. `src/lib/astro-url-scheme.test.ts` times out under full-suite load on this Windows machine; an unmodified `origin/main` worktree fails the same two cases with the same timings, so it is not this branch. Recorded on #132, which already tracks that class.
- `npm run build` — clean
- brand-literal lint — no name, host or colour literal in any changed file, and none of them carries a budget entry
- `lint-refs.sh` on the branch and over the range, `lint-commit-authors.sh` over the range"""
io.open('/tmp/pr554.json','w',encoding='utf-8').write(json.dumps({
  "title": "The cashback types say what the api actually sends",
  "head": "xcoder/cashback-contract-truth",
  "base": "main",
  "body": body,
}))
print("ok")
PYEOF
